payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the Way; the Name that can be named is not the Name; the Nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth, the Name is the mother of all things. The constant absence of desire allows one to see the wonderful; the constant desire allows one to see the boundary. These two are of the same origin but different names. They are called the Void. The Void is again and again the Void. The Gate of the Many Mysteries.

issues.span: the Name is the mother of all things
issues.advice: Source has 有名 (the named / having names), not 名 (the Name); render as 'the named is the mother of all things' to preserve the 無名/有名 parallel.

issues.span: The constant absence of desire allows one to see the wonderful
issues.advice: 常無欲 modifies the subject's state ('always without desire'), not 'constant absence of desire'; also 妙 is 'subtlety/wonder' — consider 'always without desire, one observes its subtlety'.

issues.span: the constant desire allows one to see the boundary
issues.advice: Parallel to previous: 'always having desire, one observes its manifestations/outward boundary' (徼 = border/manifestation).

issues.span: They are called the Void
issues.advice: 同謂之玄 — 玄 is 'the dark/mystery/profound', not 'Void'; render as 'both are called the profound/mystery'.

issues.span: The Void is again and again the Void
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'profound and ever more profound', not a repetition of 'Void'; correct to reflect deepening mystery.

issues.span: The Gate of the Many Mysteries.
issues.advice: Fragment lacks a verb and is disconnected; integrate as 'the gate to all mysteries' (衆妙 = all subtleties/marvels).

issues.span: the wonderful
issues.advice: 妙 is conventionally rendered 'subtlety' or 'wonder/marvel'; 'the wonderful' is awkward as a noun.

issues.span: The profound is again and again the profound.

issues.span: the named is the mother of all things

payload.translation: Le savoir peut être dit, et ce qui est dit n'est pas le même savoir; le nom peut être nommé, et ce qui est nommé n'est pas le même nom. Le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses et la mère des choses; le nom a des choses. Il faut souvent se désintéresser pour observer la subtilité, et souvent se désintéresser pour observer les limites. Ces deux sont d'une seule origine mais ont des noms différents. On les appelle le Sombre. Le Sombre est encore le Sombre. La porte des choses infiniment subtiles.

issues.span: le nom a des choses

issues.span: Ces deux sont d'une seule origine mais ont des noms différents
issues.advice: Acceptable, but 同出而異名 refers to the two aspects emerging together with different names; ensure 同謂之玄 ('both called the mystery') is rendered as a shared designation, not a separate sentence.

payload.translation: 道は言及せず、道は非道である。名は言及せず、名は非名である。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物的母である。常無を欲せず、妙を観ず。常欲を欲せず、徼を観ず。これら二つは同一の源から出ているが異名である。これを玄と呼ぶ。玄は玄であり、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。

issues.span: 道は言及せず、道は非道である
issues.advice: The source means 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao' (道可道非常道), not 'do not mention the Dao; the Dao is non-Dao'. Render the conditional/relative sense: '道として語りうる道は、常の道ではない'.

issues.span: 名は言及せず、名は非名である
issues.advice: Source 名可名非常名 means 'the name that can be named is not the constant name', not 'do not mention the name; the name is non-name'. Use '名として名づけうる名は、常の名ではない'.

issues.span: 常無を欲せず、妙を観ず。常欲を欲せず、徼を観ず
issues.advice: Source 常無欲以觀其妙 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly without desire, one observes its wonder; constantly with desire, one observes its manifestations'. The translation negates the desire and misreads the structure. Render as '常に無欲にしてその妙を観、常に有欲にしてその徼を観る'.

issues.span: 玄は玄であり、玄之又玄
issues.advice: Source 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' (deepening mystery), not 'the mystery is mystery; mystery again mystery'. Render as '玄のまた玄'.

issues.span: 万物的母
issues.advice: This is not idiomatic Japanese and mixes Chinese; use '万物の母'.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物的母である
issues.advice: Source 無名天地之始 有名萬物之母: 'the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of all things'. Keep the parallel and use '無名は天地の始、有名は万物の母'.

issues.span: これら二つは同一の源から出ているが異名である
issues.advice: Source 此兩者同出而異名 means 'these two emerge together but have different names'. '同一の源から出ている' is acceptable but '同出にして異名' is closer; also the following 同謂之玄 should be 'これを同じく玄と謂う'.

issues.span: 道は言及せず
issues.advice: Classical Daoist register is lost; the translation reads as modern prohibitive prose. Preserve the aphoristic, paradoxical style of the Daodejing.

payload.translation: 道として語りうる道は、常の道ではない。名として名づけうる名は、常の名ではない。無名は天地の始、有名は万物の母。常に無欲にしてその妙を観、常に有欲にしてその徼を観る。これら二つは同出にして異名なり。これを同じく玄と謂う。玄のまた玄。衆妙の門。

issues.span: 常の道ではない
issues.advice: 「常」はここでは「恒常」の意。日本語の道徳経訳では「恒の道」または「常なる道」とし、「常の道」は不自然で意味が取りにくい。

issues.span: 無名は天地の始、有名は万物の母
issues.advice: 「無名」「有名」は名詞句として「名なきもの」「名あるもの」と訳すのが通例。漢語のまま残すと日本語として意味が不明瞭。

issues.span: 徼
issues.advice: 「徼」は難読漢字で、日本語訳では「端（はし）」「境界」「顕れ」などと訳出するのが一般的。原文の漢字をそのまま残すと読者に伝わらない。

issues.span: 道は言うる道は恒なる道ではない
issues.advice: The first clause '道可道' means 'the Way that can be spoken/expressed', not 'the Way that speaks'. The rendering '言うる' is ambiguous; consider '道というべき道' or '言い表せる道' to convey 'can be spoken'.

issues.span: 恒なる
issues.advice: '常' in the Daodejing is conventionally rendered '恒' or '常' as 'eternal/constant'; '恒なる' is acceptable but the standard Japanese philosophical rendering is '常なる' or '恒常なる'. Ensure consistency with the established Daodejing terminology.

issues.advice: The source '常無欲以觀其妙' means 'constantly without desire, thereby observe its subtlety'; the translation is acceptable but 'にして' slightly shifts the causal/instrumental '以'. Minor.

issues.span: 徼
issues.advice: '徼' (jiao) is conventionally rendered '徼' or '境界/端' in Japanese Daodejing translations; retaining the character is fine but a gloss may aid comprehension.

payload.translation: The highest virtue is like water; water benefits all things without striving. It dwells where others find no place, is good at the deep, and is kind to all. issues.span: is kind to all

payload.translation: Carrying wealth to excess is not as good as having it at hand; sharpening it is not as secure as keeping it; gold and jade are filled with treasures, yet no one can guard them; to be rich and proud is to lose one's own fault; when merit and fame are achieved, one retires. issues.advice: The source 持而盈之 means 'to hold and fill to overflowing'; it is not about 'carrying wealth' or 'having it at hand'. Render as holding/filling to excess being worse than stopping.

issues.span: gold and jade are filled with treasures, yet no one can guard them
issues.advice: 金玉滿堂 means 'gold and jade fill the hall', not 'gold and jade are filled with treasures'. Subject/object are inverted.

issues.span: to be rich and proud is to lose one's own fault
issues.advice: 自遺其咎 means 'brings disaster/blame upon oneself', not 'lose one's own fault'. The causal sense is inverted.

issues.span: when merit and fame are achieved, one retires
issues.advice: 功成名遂身退 means 'when merit is accomplished and fame achieved, withdraw the self' — acceptable, but '身退' should convey withdrawing oneself, not merely 'one retires'.

issues.span: This is the way of heaven

payload.translation: The wise in ancient times, who skillfully cultivate the way of the scholar, are subtle, mysterious, profound, and deep, beyond recognition. For it is precisely because they are beyond recognition that they are cultivated with care and grace, like a winter person crossing a river, as if they feared their four neighbors, standing like guests, scattered like mist, like ice about to melt, pure as the primitive state, vast as the wilderness, like the clear valley, all mixed with turbidity. Who can make turbidity still? Who can gradually clear it? Who can make it still and quiet? Who can make it slow and calm? Who can make it slow and long? The one who preserves this way does not desire fullness. For it is precisely because they do not desire fullness that they can endure without newness and remain unblemished.

issues.span: who skillfully cultivate the way of the scholar
issues.advice: 善為士者 means 'those who were skilled as masters/officials' — not 'cultivate the way of the scholar'. Remove the added 'cultivate the way of the scholar'.

issues.span: they are cultivated with care and grace
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe their appearance' — not 'they are cultivated with care and grace'. This is a major mistranslation.

issues.span: like a winter person crossing a river
issues.advice: 豫若冬涉川 means 'hesitant, as if crossing a river in winter' — 'winter person' is wrong; the hesitation sense is lost.

issues.span: scattered like mist
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 means 'yielding/dissolving like ice about to melt' — 'scattered like mist' is inaccurate and duplicates the ice image.

issues.span: like the clear valley
issues.advice: 曠兮其若谷 means 'open/vast like a valley' — 'clear valley' is wrong; 曠 is openness, not clarity.

issues.span: Who can make turbidity still? Who can gradually clear it? Who can make it still and quiet? Who can make it slow and calm? Who can make it slow and long?
issues.advice: The source has two rhetorical questions: 孰能濁以靜之徐清 (who can, from turbidity, still it and gradually clear it?) and 孰能安以乆動之徐生 (who can, from stability, through long movement gradually generate life?). The translation invents extra questions and loses the 動之徐生 'movement gradually producing life' meaning.

issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus they can be worn/old without needing new completion' — 'remain unblemished' is not in the source; 弊 is 'worn/old', not 'unblemished'.

issues.span: the primitive state
issues.advice: 樸 is conventionally 'uncarved block' — a key Daoist term; 'primitive state' loses the technical sense.

issues.span: the way of the scholar
issues.advice: 士 here is 'master/official/gentleman', not 'scholar'; and 道 as 'the Way' should be capitalized consistently as a technical term.

payload.translation: Ceux qui savent bien faire des hommes sont subtils, mystérieux, profonds et inconnus. payload.translation: 古に優れた士の人は微妙玄通深不可知である。そのようにして認識できないからこそ、強いてその容姿を豊かにし、安らぎとしよう。冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客を待たし、氷が解けるように、朴（くろ）をなぞる。広大であるがゆえに谷のように、混濁であるがゆえに濁りない。誰が静かにして濁り、徐々にして清らかにする。誰が動かし、徐々にして安らぎに保つ。この道に優れた者は、盈（ふん）を求めない。なぜなら、不盈であるからこそ、弊（ひ）を成し、新（しん）を成すことができる。

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been more than two years. Yet, while I am writing, I am constantly recalling the past, which shows that I am not a man of 'establishing a legacy.' For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man; thus, people write to immortalize, and the immortalized person writes to be immortalized. Ultimately, it is unclear who is writing for whom, and finally, it all comes down to writing about Ah Q, as if there were ghosts in my thoughts.

issues.span: it has been more than two years
issues.advice: The source says '已经不止一两年了' meaning 'more than one or two years' (i.e., several years), not 'more than two years'; render as 'more than a year or two'.

issues.span: while I am writing, I am constantly recalling the past
issues.advice: '一面要做，一面又往回想' means while intending to write, I keep having second thoughts / hesitating, not 'recalling the past'; revise to convey hesitation/reconsideration.

issues.span: a man of 'establishing a legacy'
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian term meaning 'to establish words/teachings that endure' (one of the three immortalities); render as 'a man who establishes enduring words' or similar, not 'establishing a legacy'.

issues.span: people write to immortalize, and the immortalized person writes to be immortalized
issues.advice: The source '人以文传，文以人传' means 'the man is transmitted through his writing, and the writing is transmitted through the man' — a mutual transmission, not 'people write to immortalize'; revise to reflect 'man is handed down by his writing, writing by the man'.

issues.span: who is writing for whom
issues.advice: '究竟谁靠谁传' means 'who relies on whom to be transmitted/handed down', not 'who is writing for whom'; correct the sense of 传 as transmission.

issues.span: as if there were ghosts in my thoughts
issues.advice: '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' idiomatically means 'as if something were haunting my mind' or 'as if a ghost were in my head'; the current phrasing is awkward.

issues.span: I am writing a biography of Ah Q
issues.advice: The source says 我要给阿Q做正传 (I want to write a proper biography of Ah Q), expressing intent/desire rather than an ongoing action; consider rendering the volitional sense.

issues.span: it has been more than a year or two
issues.advice: The source 已经不止一两年了 means the intention has lasted more than a year or two; the English reads as if the writing itself has lasted that long. Clarify that the desire/intention has been there for over a year or two.

issues.span: a man of establishing enduring words
issues.advice: 『立言』 is a classical Confucian concept (establishing words that endure); the literal rendering is awkward. Consider a more idiomatic gloss such as 'one who establishes lasting words' or an explanatory rendering.

issues.span: an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man
issues.advice: The source 从来不朽之笔，须传不朽之人 means an immortal pen must transmit/hand down an immortal person, not 'immortalize' (make immortal). Use 'transmit' or 'hand down' to match 传.

issues.span: the man is handed down through his writing, and the writing is handed down through the man
issues.advice: The source 人以文传，文以人传 is a chiastic parallel; the rendering is acceptable but could preserve the parallel more tightly. Minor.

issues.span: Ultimately, it is unclear who relies on whom to be transmitted, and finally, it all comes down to writing about Ah Q
issues.advice: Two 'finally/ultimately' adverbs in one sentence create redundancy; smooth the flow.

issues.span: as if something were haunting my thoughts
issues.advice: 仿佛思想里有鬼似的 literally suggests 'as if there were a ghost in my thoughts'; 'haunting my thoughts' is a reasonable idiomatic rendering, but consider preserving the ghost image more explicitly.

issues.span: I am writing a proper biography of Ah Q
issues.advice: The source says 我要给阿Q做正传 ('I want to write a proper biography of Ah Q'), expressing intention, not an action already in progress. Render as 'I want to write' / 'I have wanted to write' to match the tense and the following clause about long-standing intention.

issues.span: while I am writing, I am constantly second-guessing myself
issues.advice: 一面要做，一面又往回想 means 'while wanting to do it, I keep turning it over in my mind / having second thoughts' — the aspect is habitual intention, not simultaneous ongoing writing. Adjust to reflect 'while wanting to do it, I keep reflecting back' rather than present progressive writing.

issues.span: a man of establishing enduring words
issues.advice: 『立言』 is a classical Confucian concept (establishing words that endure, one of the three immortalities 三不朽). The literal calque is awkward; use a recognized rendering such as 'one who establishes words (li yan)' or 'a man who establishes enduring words' with a brief gloss to preserve the allusion.

issues.span: transmit an immortal person
issues.advice: 传 here means 'to hand down / perpetuate (a person's memory)', not 'transmit a person'. Use 'to hand down an immortal person' or 'to perpetuate the memory of an immortal person' for consistency with the following 人以文传，文以人传.

issues.span: the man is handed down through his writing, and the writing is handed down through the man
issues.advice: The parallel 人以文传，文以人传 is a compact chiasmus; the English is wordy and loses the rhetorical balance. Tighten to something like 'the man is handed down by his writing, the writing by the man' to preserve the symmetry.

issues.span: as if something were haunting my thoughts
issues.advice: 仿佛思想里有鬼似的 literally means 'as if there were a ghost in my thoughts' — the ghost image is deliberate and comic-gothic. 'Something haunting' is acceptable but weakens the concrete 鬼; consider 'as if a ghost were in my thoughts' to keep the image.

payload.translation: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat vague; even his former deeds are vague. For the people of Weizhuang, as to Aq, as long as he helps them, they only take him for a joke, and never pay attention to his deeds. And Aq himself does not say so, but only when he has a quarrel with others, he sometimes squints his eyes and says: "We were once much more superior to you! What sort of thing are you?"

issues.span: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat vague
issues.advice: The opening is ungrammatical and misparses the source; render as 'Not only are Aq's name and native place somewhat vague' to preserve the 'not only... even...' structure.

issues.span: they only take him for a joke
issues.advice: The source means they merely use him for amusement/teasing; 'take him for a joke' is ambiguous—use 'only make fun of him' or 'only use him as a butt of jokes'.

issues.span: he sometimes squints his eyes
issues.advice: 瞪着眼睛 means 'glare' or 'stare wide-eyed,' not 'squint'; correct to 'glare' or 'open his eyes wide'.

issues.span: We were once much more superior to you!
issues.advice: '阔' here means wealthy/prosperous, not 'superior'; render as 'We were once much richer than you!'

issues.span: Weizhuang
issues.advice: The village name 未庄 is conventionally rendered 'Weizhuang' but should be consistent with established translations; consider 'Wei Village' or keep pinyin consistently.

issues.span: as to Aq, as long as he helps them, they only take him for a joke
issues.advice: The clause chain is awkward and repetitive; restructure for natural English flow, e.g. 'the people of Weizhuang only cared that he helped them and made fun of him.'

issues.span: 行状
issues.advice: 'Deeds' is acceptable but the term carries a mock-formal, biographical connotation; consider 'exploits' or 'record' to preserve the ironic register.

payload.translation: Aq's name and native place are somewhat vague; even his former exploits are unclear. For the people of Weizhuang, as long as he helps them, they merely make fun of him and pay no attention to his deeds. Aq himself does not admit this, but whenever he has a quarrel with others, he sometimes glares and says, "We were once much richer than you! What sort of thing are you?"

issues.span: Aq himself does not admit this
issues.advice: The source says 阿Q自己也不说 ('Ah Q himself does not say/tell'), not that he 'does not admit this'. Render as 'Nor does Ah Q himself say anything about it' or similar.

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they merely make fun of him
issues.advice: The source 只要他帮忙，只拿他玩笑 means they only want him to help and only use him for jokes; the causal 'as long as' framing slightly shifts meaning. Consider 'they only wanted his help and only made fun of him'.

issues.span: exploits
issues.advice: 『行状』 (xingzhuang) is a formal term for a biographical account/conduct record; 'exploits' is misleading. Use 'biography' or 'record of his doings' consistently with the later 'deeds'.

issues.span: Weizhuang
issues.advice: 未庄 is conventionally rendered 'Weizhuang' but often as 'the village of Wei' or 'Wei Village'; ensure consistency with established translations of the text.

payload.translation: Aq's name and place of origin are somewhat obscure; even his former biography is unclear. For the people of Weizhuang, as long as he helps them, they only want him to do so and only make fun of him, never paying attention to his conduct. Aq himself does not admit this; he only speaks of it when he has a quarrel with others, sometimes glazing his eyes and saying, "We were once much richer than you! What sort of thing are you?"

issues.span: Aq himself does not admit this
issues.advice: The source says 阿Q自己也不说 ('Aq himself does not say/tell'), not that he 'does not admit this.' Render as 'Aq himself does not say so either' or 'nor does Aq himself speak of it.'

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they only want him to do so and only make fun of him
issues.advice: The source 只要他帮忙，只拿他玩笑 means they only want him to help and only make fun of him—the 'as long as' conditional is not in the source. Remove the conditional framing.

issues.span: he only speaks of it when he has a quarrel with others
issues.advice: The source 独有和别人口角的时候，间或瞪着眼睛道 means 'only when quarreling with others does he occasionally glare and say'—'间或' (occasionally) is omitted and 'only speaks of it' misrepresents the structure. Add 'occasionally.'

issues.span: glazing his eyes
issues.advice: 'Glazing his eyes' is not idiomatic; 瞪着眼睛 means 'glaring' or 'staring wide-eyed.' Use 'glaring.'

issues.span: somewhat obscure; even his former biography is unclear
issues.advice: The semicolon joining two loosely related clauses reads awkwardly; consider a period or 'and even.'
